name: Zombo.com
title: The Website That Promised You Everything
claims: Zombo.com was created in 1999 as a single-serving site | 1
The site parodies Flash introductory pages that play while the rest of a site loads | 1
Zombo took the concept to a humorous extreme: one long introductory page leading to a newsletter invitation | 1
The domain Zombo.com was registered on October 10, 1999 | 1
In 2001 the creator said "Zombo" meant a male zombie, as a friend learned in English class | 1
The creator said the word "just sort of popped up" when it was time to name the site | 1
The original page had a blank page, a colorful title and a throbber of seven colorful rapidly rotating discs that appeared to pulsate | 1
An audio clip of a man welcomed the visitor to Zombo.com (pronounced "Zombocom") and promised a place where "everything is possible" | 1
After some time a "newZletter" sign-up option appeared, parodying online newsletters | 1
The link went to join1.htm, which said the option was not available yet, as a humorous thank-you reading "ThankZ for your patience" | 1
The HTML markup contained the comment "Please Visit http://www.15footstick.com our other website ThankZ" | 1
15footstick.com had art and music and a page selling Zombo.com T-shirts, and has since gone down for maintenance | 1
A web animator chose Zombo.com as the least useful website because "it doesn't do anything except tell you how wonderful it is" | 1
A Cartoon Network senior producer cited it as least useful site two years earlier in the same column: "Utterly useless, absolutely brilliant" | 1
A PC World writer listed it among the ten most useless websites, concluding "Well, in fact, nothing happens at zombo.com" | 1
In 2004 a newspaper writer (The Advertiser) called it "the most welcoming website on the Internet" | 1
In 2007 a writer (Digital Life) called it "the ultimate time-waster" | 1
The Australian wrote "Zombo.com has just one joke, but it's a good one" | 1
A game industry figure listed Zombo.com among favorite sites in a 2002 interview, in a list of mostly webcomic, humor and entertainment sites | 2
A musician listed Zombo as his favorite website, saying it "paraphrases the net" and "promises you the earth but delivers a bit of animation with a scratchy soundtrack" | 1
On 4 September 2013 a webcomic creator listed Zombo.com as his favorite website in an interview with Runner's World | 1
Zombo.com was featured on Neal.fun's Internet Artifacts | 1
On 23 January 2020 a game programmer created a VR version of Zombo.com | 1
The site was initially Flash and switched to HTML5 due to Adobe Flash Player's discontinuation on December 1, 2020 | 1
In the HTML5 version the audio loops to the start, removing the newZletter message; the HTML comment was removed; discs spin at a smoother frame rate and look less like they change color | 1
On February 7, 2026 the domain redirected to a GoDaddy page listing Zombo.com for sale; the redirect was quickly removed | 1
Over the following days the banner, audio and UI were redesigned | 1
On February 9 the most recent change added text welcoming the user to "New Management" and saying the new owner was interested in purchasing the rights to the original content from its owners | 1
Several fan-made websites have since emerged recreating the original content | 1
Wayback Machine archives of the Flash version (1999-11-28) and HTML version (2025-03-21) exist | 1
